ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three horizontal line segments, and they are all marked as parallel with arrows in the same direction. The two left and right slanted sides are also marked as parallel with arrows in the same direction. Near the intersection of the middle horizontal line and the right slanted side, the angle (4x−5)° is marked; near the intersection of the bottom horizontal line and the right slanted side, the angle (3x+11)° is marked; near the intersection of the middle horizontal line and the left slanted side, the angle (3y+1)° is marked. Reasoning: Because the middle horizontal line and the bottom horizontal line are parallel, when the right slanted side is used as a transversal, (4x−5)° and (3x+11)° are corresponding angles, so they are equal: 4x−5 = 3x+11, solving gives x = 16. Therefore (4x−5)° = 4(16)−5 = 59°. Also because the left and right slanted sides are parallel, when the middle horizontal line is used as a transversal, (3y+1)° and 59° are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary: (3y+1)+59 = 180. Thus 3y+60 = 180, 3y = 120, y = 40.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as three horizontal segments marked parallel and two slanted side segments also marked parallel. Use the right slanted side as a transversal across the middle and bottom parallel horizontal lines: the angles labeled (4x−5)° and (3x+11)° occupy corresponding positions, so set 4x−5 = 3x+11 to get x = 16 and hence (4x−5)° = 59°. Then use the middle horizontal segment as a transversal across the two parallel slanted sides: the angles labeled (3y+1)° and 59° are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary. Solve (3y+1)+59 = 180, giving 3y = 120 and y = 40.
